name: Puerto Rico (US)
governmentType: unincorporated organized territory of the US with local self-government; republican form of territorial government with separate executive, legislative, and judicial branches; note - reference Puerto Rican Federal Relations Act, 2 March 1917, as amended by Public Law 600, 3 July 1950
independence: none (territory of the US with commonwealth status)

indicators.indicator: Political stability and absence of violence

partiesListed.party: Citizens' Victory Movement (Movimiento Victoria Ciudadana) or MVC
New Progressive Party or PNP (pro-US statehood)
Puerto Rican Independence Party or PIP (pro-independence)

profile.religions: Roman Catholic 56%, Protestant 33% (largely Pentecostal), other 2%, atheist 1%, none 7% (2014 est.)
profile.legalSystem: civil law system based on the Spanish civil code, within the framework of the US federal system
profile.independence: none (territory of the US with commonwealth status)
profile.nationalHoliday: US Independence Day, 4 July (1776); Puerto Rico Constitution Day, 25 July (1952)
profile.location: Caribbean, island between the Caribbean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean, east of the Dominican Republic
